corrections.text: The summary says one CVE "reached Ubuntu 25 days after Debian's advisory". The 25 days run from Debian's DSA-6568-1 (October 16) to Ubuntu's stable-update notices dated November 10 (the Herald's count); OMG! Ubuntu reports that, as of November 3, patched kernels for CVE-2026-98432 were in testing for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 LTS (18 days after Debian's advisory, the Herald's count). USN-9024-1 and USN-9025-1, whose 3,276 and 3,498 distinct CVE identifiers the article cites, each cover specific kernel flavours for Ubuntu 24.04 and 22.04 only.

The article says Tom's Hardware quotes Linus Torvalds "saying that in the BPF area AI fixes outnumbered reports". Tom's Hardware attributes that statement to a note from BPF maintainer Alexei Starovoitov, which Torvalds relayed in his 7.4-rc2 message; the quotation "most other areas haven't reached that point yet, but it's at least a sign that we may be starting to see the tide starting to turn" is Torvalds' own.

The article says the OpenJDK advisories of October 21 and October 24 each cover one CVE and point readers to an eMudhra page. Those two advisory pages are not among the article's cited sources; the cited index page lists only their dates. The Herald's reviewer read them: each lists one CVE (CVE-2026-91403 and CVE-2026-114820) and says "Please see openjdk.org/emudhra".
